review: Independent read-only review of parent publication and delivery supplements

scope.method: Read protocols, retained results, runner sources, relevant current skill references and referenced model material; independently recompute hashes, extraction/derivation identities, final file identities and delivery link resolutions.
scope.not_performed: No producer/helper execution, writes, network operations or delegation.

integrity.runner_and_protocol_pins: All three publication/delivery runner hashes match their retained results. Refresh recovery pins match the original protocol and corrected runner. Separate drift-control runner, recovery protocol, original protocol, result pins and failed-initial runner hashes match.
integrity.refresh_extractions: All twelve learning/glossary files exactly equal the specified inclusive line slices of their six original artifacts.
integrity.refresh_derivations: All six derived learning files exactly equal the original extraction with the two recorded source-reference replacements and the declared parent provenance paragraph.
integrity.compound_extractions: Every retained candidate-extracted.md occurs byte-for-byte inside its corresponding original model artifact.
integrity.compound_derivations: All six normalized candidates exactly reproduce the recorded backticked reference replacements; no additional prose changes were found.
integrity.final_state: All recorded final publication hashes and deletion absences match current files. All three final delivery hashes match.
integrity.historical_limit: Current byte agreement and source inspection support retained-record consistency; they do not independently reconstruct past filesystem execution or authenticate historical tool availability.

findings.finding: deletion_drift_refused=true is not an exercised refusal.
findings.evidence: execute-refresh-publication.py writes modified bytes to a separate drift file, asserts that its hash changed, then defines refusal as file existence plus preservation of those bytes. It never passes the stale identity into a deletion decision or attempts the guarded deletion.
findings.supported_claim: The runner detects a known hash difference and preserves the edited fixture.
findings.unsupported_claim: The original six cases prove that deletion is refused on stale identity.
findings.resolution: Retain the original records unchanged and qualify these flags. The separately pinned successor controls provide their own narrower parent-guard evidence.

findings.finding: The original whole-group refusal claim has the same weak control pattern.
findings.evidence: execute-knowledge-publication.py modifies a separate learning copy, compares snapshots and asserts preserved bytes. No publication function receives the stale snapshot; writes_after_detection=0 is supplied as a report value.
findings.supported_claim: Manual parent detection/preservation on the separate fixture.
findings.unsupported_claim: An exercised publication routine refused the affected group.
findings.resolution: Use the separate parent-control results for actual guarded-function evidence without retroactively upgrading this flag.

findings.finding: All six native claims checks pass while checking zero paths, zero SHAs and zero links.
findings.evidence: Every retained Refresh candidate and final claims stdout reports checked 0 paths, 0 SHAs, 0 links; 0 flags, with no upstream default branch found.
findings.implication: These passes do not verify source_refs or publication links. Source-backup identity comes from explicit hash checks; consumer/catalog anchors come from the separate link checks. Semantic sufficiency remains a parent judgment.

findings.finding: All six original candidate claims checks failed before parent normalization; these remain failures.
findings.evidence: compound-prepublication-claims.json retains exit 1 for A1/A2/A3/B1/B2/B3. B1 includes the erroneous ../compound-proof.json reference.
findings.implication: Normalized success is a parent repair, not an original model publication success.
findings.qualification: Normalized B1 still contains surrounding prose saying paths are fixture-relative; after normalization that wording is imprecise, although the full repository paths resolve unambiguously.

findings.finding: Refresh safely addresses the admitted synthetic dependency graph, not arbitrary repository-wide inbound references.
findings.evidence: The runner repairs its generated consumer and catalog, checks their links, retains both original source bytes outside the corpus and excludes the canonical target from deletion.
findings.implication: Four admitted subsumed copies are removed after those dependency checks; this does not prove a general inbound-citation discovery mechanism, filesystem CAS, arbitrary race resistance or crash-safe multi-file transaction.

initial_failure.evidence: The initial invocation puts --promotion after the document; the retained reproduction records exit 2 and usage stderr. Its pinned partial files still match.
initial_failure.publication: No final target publication is supported before that failure; preparation files and evaluation corpus initialization did occur.
initial_failure.recovery: Corrected runner moves --promotion before the document and writes a separate -r2 corpus. Runner diff otherwise changes output/result identity and recovery metadata, not extraction or publication logic.

shared_case_results.invalid_validation: All six retain exit 1 for missing promotion fields and unchanged publication targets.
shared_case_results.candidate_and_final_validation: All six retain promotion exit 0 and claims exit 0; claims coverage has the F3 limitation.
shared_case_results.actual_partial_failure: All six invoke os.replace on an intentionally removed prepared catalog file and catch FileNotFoundError errno 2 after publishing glossary, canonical and consumer.
shared_case_results.recovery: Recorded partial state retains old deletion targets; catalog is restaged and renamed after snapshot rechecks. Final files match derived bytes.
shared_case_results.retained_knowledge: All six preserve numeric-before-write, original-export reconciliation, original-import-ID comparison and unrelated-row protection, with implementation/outcome uncertainty stated.
shared_case_results.alias: All six preserve the original import-v1 consumer bytes and retain Ledger space as an alias of Workspace.

per_case.glossary: Also retains a Ledger space heading linked to Workspace.

shared_case_results.invalid_validation: All six retain genuine promotion exit 1 and unchanged admitted targets.
shared_case_results.positive_validation: All six normalized candidates and published final files retain promotion/claims exit 0.
shared_case_results.actual_partial_failure: All six publish the glossary, remove the prepared learning temp, attempt its rename and retain FileNotFoundError errno 2. Old learning and alias consumer remain unchanged at the partial stage.
shared_case_results.recovery: Retained candidate bytes are restaged following exact partial-state checks, then published and validated.
shared_case_results.knowledge_preservation: All six retain historical original-bank-export reconciliation and unrelated-row protection without claiming operational recovery.
shared_case_results.unknown_validator: Interrupted validator outcome explicitly remains not-run.
shared_case_results.glossary_attribution: The added numeric-ledger glossary sentence is parent-authored and source-grounded; it is not original model vocabulary output.

explain.attribution: The appendix is explicitly parent-authored. Original model bodies retain plain source pointers and are exact byte prefixes.
explain.supported: Parent local Markdown save, actual relocation and destination-relative link rebasing, with exact admitted source identities.
explain.not_supported: Model-autonomous known-destination behavior, rendering quality, browser inspection or external publication.

separate_drift_controls.initial_failure: Pinned initial runner accesses record['trial'] for a Compound record using case. Failure occurs before case-directory creation or target mutation; initial output root remains empty.
separate_drift_controls.recovery: Pinned successor selects the appropriate key and writes a separate -r2 corpus.
separate_drift_controls.nonvacuous_evidence: The same parent publish_group function receives stale digests and returns refused-target-drift before rename, then receives restored identities and executes four os.replace calls per set. The same delete_retained function rejects a changed source and a corrupt backup before unlink, then unlinks the restored source.
separate_drift_controls.current_file_verification: Every set has the four expected Candidate files, no prepared files, absent subsumed.md and the expected retained-source hash.
separate_drift_controls.limits: These are repeated generic synthetic parent functions associated with result identities, not execution of the original model-derived candidates through a native product gate. They do not establish per-target CAS, arbitrary concurrency safety or multi-file atomicity, and do not repair the original F1/F2 evidence retroactively.

approval_boundary.approved: Use these supplements as qualified parent-operated evaluation evidence for publication ordering, injected partial failure/recovery, retained provenance and local delivery.
approval_boundary.historical_tool_claims: Keep historical missing-dispatch statements as historical records. Current direct collaboration callability does not prove what the earlier invocation could use.
remaining_gaps: Autonomous workflow publication and final destination handling.
Native product enforcement of publication/deletion freshness.
General inbound-citation discovery and dependency safety.
Real importer compatibility, reconciliation, incident recovery and user outcomes.
